text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Police in Blantyre's township of Ndirande arrested a man for vote rigging, bringing the number to seven those arrested since last week for rigging while preparing for by-elections to be held on November 19.

- The Supreme Court of Appeal has allowed British lawyers to assist government in an appeal case against main opposition party Malawi Congress Party (MCP) in a tug-of-war for former president Kamuzu Banda's conglomerate, Press Trust.
- President Bakili Muluzi has extended an invitation to opposition parties to work together by offering alternative solutions to the country's economic and political problems instead of criticisms.

- The main opposition MCP has lodged a complaint to the Electoral Commission that the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) party was ferrying people from other constituencies to register in Ndirande, in Blantyre in preparation for the November 19, by-lections.
- President Bakili Muluzi made a surprise statement that he is now willing to work with the opposition parties including those outside parliament.

- Victims of the political atrocities committed by the former regime of Kamuzu Banda, who hoped the National Compensation Tribunal would assist them, continue to silently suffer. Many of the victims are aged and risk dying before they receive full compensation.
